Add habitat zones to a Habitat object

Source: R/habitat.R
add_habitat.Rd

Add habitat zones to a Habitat object

Usage

add_habitat(hab, sf_data, weight = 1, priority = NULL, touches = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

hab

A Habitat object

sf_data

An sf object containing geometries to add

weight

A weight to apply on the habitat feature. Can then be used as resistance for dispersal functions for instance.

priority

Stacking order of the added layer when the habitat is rasterized with habitat_raster: where layers overlap, the one with the highest priority gives its value to the pixel. A single number for the whole layer, or one value per feature. By default (NULL) the layer is placed on top of everything already in hab (highest priority so far + 1), so that layers stack in the order they are added.

touches

Logical, a single value for the whole layer or one value per feature. If TRUE (default), the features fill every pixel they touch when rasterized with habitat_raster; if FALSE, a polygon only fills the pixels whose centre it covers, and a line only the pixels of a thin line. See Details.

...

Additional arguments

Value

A Habitat object with new geometries added as habitat

Details

touches controls which pixels a feature occupies, not how hard it is to cross: the permeability of a structure is carried by its weight (or by add_nohabitat for an absolute barrier).

  • touches = TRUE keeps thin structures (hedgerows, rivers, roads, whether drawn as lines or as narrow polygons) continuous: every pixel they cross is filled, so they cannot vanish between pixel centres nor be crossed diagonally between two pixels. The price is a footprint larger than the feature: it grows by up to one pixel in width.

  • touches = FALSE keeps areas unbiased, which is preferable for a layer made of contiguous polygons covering the whole landscape (a land cover map): with touches = TRUE, each polygon would spread on the pixels of its neighbours and the border pixels would go to the feature on top of the stack.

A common set-up is therefore a land cover layer added with touches = FALSE and a low priority, with the thin structures that must stay continuous added on top with touches = TRUE.

Examples

library(sf)
#> Linking to GEOS 3.12.1, GDAL 3.8.4, PROJ 9.4.0; sf_use_s2() is TRUE
square <- function(a, b) {
  st_sf(geometry = st_sfc(st_polygon(list(
    cbind(c(a, b, b, a, a), c(a, a, b, b, a))))))
}
hedge <- st_sf(geometry = st_sfc(st_linestring(cbind(c(0, 10), c(0, 10)))))

# the hedge is declared first but kept on top of the field with `priority`
hab <- habitat() |>
  add_habitat(hedge, weight = 1, priority = 10) |>
  add_habitat(square(2, 8), weight = 0.2, priority = 1)
hab

#> Number of features: 2 
#> CRS: NA 
#> Simple feature collection with 2 features and 4 fields

#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 0 ymin: 0 xmax: 10 ymax: 10
#> CRS:           NA
#>   habitat weight priority touches                       geometry
#> 1    TRUE    1.0       10    TRUE        LINESTRING (0 0, 10 10)
